overall_strategy: Mario is a 6-year-old (73-month) Golden Retriever, 30 lb, low activity and light chewer, living in an apartment with no yard and a beef allergy. At this established journey stage we prioritize reliable consumable subscriptions that match his predictable monthly needs (kibble, wet toppers, training treats, poop bags, joint supplements, calming-diffuser refills, and an optional indoor grass pad for bad weather). For each consumable I showed the math used to estimate depletion and cadence so deliveries avoid waste but prevent running out. One-time purchases focus on immediate seasonal safety (cooling pad), apartment-friendly durable essentials (stainless bowls, deshedding tool, nail grinder, orthopedic bed), and enrichment/setup items (slow feeder, treat pouch, LED leash, indoor potty system). This mix keeps Mario healthy (weight control, joint support), comfortable (cooling pad, bed), and mentally engaged (puzzle feeders, toys) while minimizing overbuying of durables and ensuring frequent items are auto-shipped on a cadence aligned with his expected consumption.
